newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: RESEARCH ALERT - Hub Power seen good buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Hub Power seen good buy.

text.p: Pakistan's blue-chip Hub Power Company Ltd is seen as an attractive buy at the current lows of the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE), a research report said on Monday.

"Hub Power...still has a lot of power left. With its debt guaranteed by the government, the World Bank and Japan's JEXIM Bank, financial risk is negligible," said International Asset Management Company Ltd (IAMC) in its quarterly research report.
Hub Power dipped 0.55 rupees, or 1.46 percent, to 37.15 on Monday in a turnover of 4.6 million shares, dealers said.
IAMC said Hub Power's weak stock price was due to market conditions and provided an excellent buying opportunity.

"Financial 1998 will be the first full year of operations with the stipulated dividend pay-outs beginning. We expect a change in international investor profile as venture capitalists reduce exposure and income-seeking funds make their entry."
IAMC said Hub Power shares, which have risen 20 percent since September, still offered an attractive return over the next 12 months.
It said the stock price had been discounted due to concerns about the ability of the state-owned Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) to fund electricity purchases from Hub Power.

"But our recent meetings with both the company as well as WAPDA lead us to believe that while there are cash flow problems, these are not unmanageable and that Hub Power is WAPDA's number one priority in terms of payments," it added.
IAMC said local and foreign investors would renew interest in the stock as Pakistan's macroeconomic position becomes clearer. "This will lead to a rerating of the stock," it said.
Its near-term cap is seen at 40 to 42 rupees, with the upside from current levels representing hefty potential capital gains, IAMC said.
It said Hub Power was expected to pay a dividend of 6.5 rupees per share by March 1998, a yield of more than 17 percent.
